title: Four lookups to read one byte: page walk, TLB, page fault, fork

glossary.note: A small CPU cache of recent page-to-frame translations.
On x86 it holds the physical address of the top-level page table.
The kernel can fill in the entry, then retry the instruction.

glossary.full: Share now, copy at the first write
glossary.note: Fork shares frames read-only; a write makes a private copy.

key_points: x86-64 with 4 KiB pages splits a 48-bit address into four 9-bit indexes and a 12-bit offset.
A TLB miss costs a page walk of up to four dependent reads; a TLB hit costs none.
A page fault is the kernel filling in a missing entry; fork plus copy-on-write copies a frame only when someone writes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ravi's program reads one byte. The CPU only has a virtual address.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Forty-eight bits: four indexes of nine bits, then a twelve bit offset into a 4 KiB page.
beats.say: Forty-eight bits: four indexes of nine bits each, then a twelve bit offset into a four kibibyte page.

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: So how does it find the page?

beats.speaker: mira
beats.text: First the TLB, a cache of finished translations. Empty, so a miss.
beats.say: First the T L B, a cache of finished translations. Empty, so a miss.

beats.speaker: mira
beats.text: A miss sends the MMU to walk the page table, starting from CR3.
beats.say: A miss sends the M M U to walk the page table, starting from C R three.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Each index picks one entry, and each entry names the next table. Four tables, four dependent RAM reads.

beats.speaker: mira
beats.text: The last entry names frame three. Frame plus offset is the physical address, and the TLB keeps it.
beats.say: The last entry names frame three. Frame plus offset is the physical address, and the T L B keeps it.

visuals.note: TLB filled: this page now translates without a walk

beats.speaker: mira
beats.text: Same page again: the TLB answers at once. No walk, no RAM reads.
beats.say: Same page again: the T L B answers at once. No walk, no RAM reads.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A brand new page is different. The first touch finds an empty entry.

beats.speaker: mira
beats.text: Not present: the CPU raises a page fault and the kernel takes over.
beats.say: Not present: the C P U raises a page fault and the kernel takes over.

beats.speaker: mira
beats.text: It picks a free frame, zeroes it, fills in the entry, and the instruction runs again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Now fork. The child gets copies of the page tables, not of the memory.

beats.speaker: mira
beats.text: Every shared frame turns read-only, marked copy-on-write.

beats.speaker: mira
beats.text: The child writes, the read-only entry faults, and the kernel copies just that frame.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The TLB hides the walk. Copy-on-write hides the copy, until a fault says otherwise.
